newsitem.title: CHINA: China bonds to be more accessible to individuals.
newsitem.headline: China bonds to be more accessible to individuals.

text.p: China is expected to issue 200 billion yuan ($24 billion) worth of non-tradeable certificate bonds and physical paper bonds in 1997, the Beijing Economic Daily said on Wednesday.
The bonds would be more accessible to individual investors, the newspaper said.
More than 50 percent of bonds issued last year were through dealing systems of the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges, making it difficult for individual investors to buy, it said.

The non-tradeable certificate bonds and physical paper bonds to be issued this year would account for about 80 percent of total treasury bonds to be issued in 1997, it said, quoting officials of the Ministry of Finance.
A ministry official said by telephone that the total bond issue had yet to be decided and needed approval by the National People's Congress, or parliament.
China issued a total of 184.779 billion yuan worth of bonds domestically in 1996, the Financial News has said.
